rows.evidence: Q1: Section 2.2 and 3 - two-year field experiment (2019-2020) at Shuguang Experimental Station, Hetao Irrigation District, with five mulch x irrigation treatments in randomized blocks, own measurements of soil/canopy temperature and humidity, photosynthesis, LAI, yield and net income.
rows.notes: The study does report its own results that plastic film mulching (transparent and black) lowered diurnal soil temperature amplitude in the 0-25 cm layer by about 0.4-1.3 C relative to unmulched full irrigation (Fig. 5, Section 3.2.2) and significantly raised canopy air relative humidity by about 4-6.5% over unmulched treatments (Fig. 2, Section 3.1.1), and lowered canopy air temperature. However, the irrigation method in all treatments was border irrigation (Section 2.2), not drip; the comparison is mulch versus no mulch under flood/border irrigation. The claim attributes the microclimate effect to drip irrigation under plastic mulch (DIPM), so the technology tested is not the one in the passage. Also, the diurnal amplitude measured is of soil temperature, not canopy air temperature. Hence Q2 is no and Q3-Q9 are not assessed.

notes: Full text appears complete (abstract through references). The study is a border-irrigated plastic film mulch trial on spring maize; drip irrigation is never used in the experiment.
